proposal.quote: We therefore consider that 200-400 operational launchers remains the best present estimate of the Soviet force in mid-1964.
proposal.rule: claude backend: The estimate's probable case for two to three years out is 150-300 ICBM launchers in mid-1963 and 200-400 in mid-1964, midpoints about 225-300 from ICBMs alone; heavy bombers and SLBMs would add to this, and nothing in the annex suggests the total reaches 1,000, so the summed force falls in the 200-999 band.

claude backend: Under the belief_force_USA rule, the estimate's probable ICBM force for two to three years out (midpoints of about 225 in mid-1963 and 300 in mid-1964) plus about 120-130 heavy bombers and tankers projected for the same dates gives a total between 200 and 999, before any submarine launchers are added.

proposal.quote: 100200 operational launchers in mid-1962, 150300 in mid-1963, and 200--400 in .mid-1964
proposal.rule: claude backend: The estimate's probable ICBM force two to three years out (about 225-300 launchers, the middle of the mid-1963 and mid-1964 ranges), plus its roughly 150 heavy bombers and tankers, sums to between 200 and 999 intercontinental vehicles.

proposal.quote: Soviet operational units were equipped with approximately 150 heavy bombers in mid-1961 ... we estimate that a gradual buildup of missile-launching ships will occur over the next five years
proposal.rule: claude backend: For mid-1963 to mid-1964, the estimate's tables project about 140-145 heavy bombers (BISON figures include tankers) plus roughly 108-126 submarine-launched missiles, summing to more than 200 before any ICBMs, which this annex omits, so the band is at least under_1000 (200 to 999). The ICBM count could raise the total, so the band is uncertain.
